findings.title: resolve() deletes valid links instead of expired ones
findings.description: The condition `Date.now() < link.expiresAt` is inverted. It deletes links that are still valid and returns undefined for them, while returning targets for expired links. This breaks the core redirect functionality.

findings.title: Quota becomes NaN for new owners
findings.description: When creating a link for a new owner, `this.quota[owner]! + 1` evaluates to `undefined + 1 = NaN` because the owner key doesn't exist yet. All quota tracking for new owners is broken.

findings.title: validate() always returns true even with problems
findings.description: The function collects validation problems and logs them, but always returns `true`. Invalid configurations (bad port, negative cache size, non-positive timeout) pass validation and the service starts in a broken state.

findings.title: requireAdmin() rejects admins due to wrong condition
findings.description: `allowed.indexOf(session.role)` returns 0 for 'admin' (first element), which is falsy. The function returns false for valid admins and true for unknown roles. Admin access control is inverted.

findings.title: bearerToken() crashes on missing Authorization header
findings.description: The function uses non-null assertion `header!` and immediately calls `.split()` on it. When Authorization header is undefined, this throws a TypeError.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS multiplied by 1000 incorrectly
findings.description: The comment states the env var is already in milliseconds, but the code multiplies by 1000, turning 30000ms into 30000000ms (8.3 hours instead of 30 seconds).

findings.title: utilization() always returns 0 when cache is not full
findings.description: The formula `Math.floor(this.entries.size / this.limit) * 100` floors before multiplying. For any size < limit, this yields 0. A 50% full cache reports 0%.

findings.title: keys() uses for...in on a Map which doesn't work
findings.description: `for (const key in this.entries)` iterates over object properties, not Map entries. This will return an empty array. The admin view cannot see cached codes.

findings.title: warmCache() returns before async probes complete
findings.description: Using `forEach` with async callbacks doesn't await the promises. The function returns immediately without waiting for probes or cache sets to complete.

findings.title: prune() returns wrong count
findings.description: The function tracks `removed` but returns `this.links.size`, reporting the remaining count instead of how many were pruned. Dashboard metrics are incorrect.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT parsed but never assigned
findings.description: The value is parsed into `limit`, checked if positive, then voided. The config's fetchLimit field never gets updated from the environment.

findings.title: page() sets end index out of bounds
findings.description: When offset + size exceeds array length, `end` is set to `all.length + 1`, which is beyond the array. slice() tolerates this but the logic is wrong.

findings.title: rename() validates 'from' twice, never validates 'to'
findings.description: Line 57-58 calls `validateCode(from)` twice. The 'to' parameter is never validated, allowing invalid codes to be created via rename.

findings.title: stats() produces NaN when store is empty
findings.description: Dividing `store.totalHits() / store.size()` when size is 0 produces NaN, corrupting the stats response.

findings.title: Async forEach does not wait for promises
findings.description: The warmCache function uses forEach with an async callback, which does not wait for the promises to resolve. The function returns immediately before any probe completes, and errors in probes are unhandled. The caller believes warming is complete when it is not.

findings.title: Quota increment is a data race
findings.description: The quota increment `this.quota[owner] = this.quota[owner]! + 1` is a read-modify-write operation on shared mutable state. Concurrent create() calls for the same owner can lose increments, corrupting quota tracking.

findings.title: Cache class has data races on shared state
findings.description: The Cache class exposes entries, timers, and hits maps without synchronization. Concurrent get/set/delete calls can corrupt the maps or lose timer registrations. The delete() method at line 64-66 does not clear the timer from the timers map, causing timer leaks.

findings.title: Shared global state accessed by concurrent request handlers
findings.description: The handle() function and its helpers access store, cache, auth, and metrics from concurrent requests without synchronization. Metrics counters (resolved, created) are incremented without atomic operations, and store/cache mutations can race.

findings.title: Authenticator sessions map has data races
findings.description: The sessions Map is accessed by issue(), verify(), and revoke() without synchronization. Concurrent token verification and revocation can cause verify() to return stale data or miss a revocation.

findings.title: keys() iterates Map incorrectly with for...in
findings.description: The keys() method uses `for (const key in this.entries)` which iterates object properties, not Map entries. This returns an empty array since Map objects don't expose keys via for...in. Should use `for (const key of this.entries.keys())`.

findings.title: Hardcoded default secret enables authentication bypass
findings.description: The Authenticator uses 'dev-secret-do-not-use' as the default secret when LINKD_SECRET is not set. In any deployment where this environment variable is not explicitly configured, attackers can forge valid tokens or predict the secret.

findings.title: Predictable session tokens using Math.random()
findings.description: Session tokens are generated using Math.random() concatenated with a timestamp. Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and its output can be predicted, allowing attackers to forge valid session tokens.

findings.title: Inverted admin authorization check
findings.description: The requireAdmin function checks `if (allowed.indexOf(session.role))` which returns -1 (truthy) when the role is NOT in the allowed list. This means non-admin roles pass the check while admin roles fail, completely inverting the authorization logic.

findings.title: Path traversal in CSV export endpoint
findings.description: The exportCsv function uses the user-controlled 'name' parameter directly in the file path without sanitization. An attacker can write files anywhere on the filesystem using paths like '../../../etc/passwd' or overwrite critical files.

findings.title: Open redirect vulnerability in /out endpoint
findings.description: The /out endpoint redirects to any URL provided in the 'next' query parameter without validation. Attackers can craft links that appear legitimate but redirect users to phishing sites or malware.

findings.title: Predictable short codes using Math.random()
findings.description: The newCode function generates short codes using Math.random(), which is not cryptographically secure. Attackers can enumerate or predict valid short codes to access or manipulate links they do not own.

findings.title: CORS misconfiguration exposes credentials
findings.description: The response sets 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' together with 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'. This combination is rejected by browsers for security reasons, but if exploited could allow any origin to access credentialed responses.

findings.title: Admin endpoint protected only by spoofable header
findings.description: The /admin/quotas endpoint checks only the 'x-admin' header which can be set by any client. There is no actual verification that the requester has admin privileges beyond the session role check.

findings.title: Missing null check on Authorization header causes crash
findings.description: The bearerToken function calls header!.split() without checking if header is undefined. A request without an Authorization header will crash the server.

findings.title: Inverted expiry logic deletes valid links
findings.description: The resolve function checks `if (Date.now() < link.expiresAt)` and deletes the link if true. This deletes NON-expired links and returns the target for expired ones, inverting the intended behavior.
